subject: Pre-commit sizing: traffic/latency profile & MVP burst plan
messages:
From: Cara Diaz <cara@syncstream.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Pre-commit sizing: traffic/latency profile & MVP burst plan

Hi Marissa / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're getting close to a pre-commit decision and procurement asked for a short, concrete sizing worksheet so they can run the numbers for GPU budget + cost approvals. High level context: we plan to launch a conversational analytics MVP in Q4 with a web frontend and API backends. Expected initial traffic is modest but with frequent 10-15 minute “event” windows where latency must remain low during product demos and peak user events.

Quick asks:
- Can you confirm what fleet footprint Redwood would recommend for an MVP that handles ~250 concurrent sessions at p95 < 400ms (generation only) with average prompt length ~120 tokens and average response ~300 tokens?
- What are your assumptions on session affinity vs stateless routing for that profile?
- We can share a short sample of recent traffic (anonymized). Would that help refine GPU sku / reserved capacity rec?

I can share the anonymized token-level samples if that helps — attaching a short summary of our current peak day counts in the email that follows.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if it speeds things up.

Best,
Cara
Cara Diaz
Head of Platform
SyncStream AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Cara Diaz <cara@syncstream.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pre-commit sizing: traffic/latency profile & MVP burst plan

Cara — thanks for the clear ask and the context. We can definitely size an initial reserved pool and provide a fallback plan for demo bursts. To make the recommendation precise we typically need:

1) Token distribution sample (prompt/response) by percentile (p50/p90/p99). A 2–3 hour sample from a peak day is ideal.
2) Concurrency model: are sessions long-lived websockets (stateful + KV cache) or stateless API calls per request?
3) Acceptable cold-start/backfill behavior for p99 — is a small percentage of elevated latency during burst acceptable?

If you can attach the sample CSV and note whether KV-cache is required for the conversation context, we’ll run it through our quick-sizer and reply with two options:
- Small reserved pool (cost-optimized) + hosted fallback for spikes
- Medium reserved pool sized for demo SLAs (guaranteed p95 target)

I’ve looped Karthik and Ben for the technical sizing and cost model respectively. I’ll aim to get a preliminary sizing back by Thu.

Attachments: none on this message.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pre-commit sizing: traffic/latency profile & MVP burst plan

Marissa / team — internal notes / probe questions before we run the script:

- Prompt mix: are there many short template prompts (e.g., 20–60 tokens) mixed with occasional long retrieval prompts (>500 tokens)? That affects per-token kernel selection.
- Response generation mode: do you require streaming token delivery to the UI (we treat streaming differently in batch windows)?
- Session affinity: for a conversational analytics MVP, KV caching of the last 2–4 turns will likely reduce per-token cost and tail latency, but it changes sizing because GPU memory per-session increases. Need an estimated average KV size per session (in tokens).
- SLA: confirm that p95 < 400ms is for generation-only (model step) vs end-to-end (including network + app).

If SyncStream can provide: 1) a small sample CSV with rows: timestamp, session_id, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, streaming_bool — we can map it to expected GPU occupancy.

Karthik / Ben — when you have a moment, I think we should produce both a conservative and an aggressive fleet map (e.g., n1: baseline reserved gpus; n2: reserved + burst apron) with cost differentials. I’ll take the customer-facing writeup.

-Laura

From: Cara Diaz <cara@syncstream.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@syncstream.ai, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pre-commit sizing: traffic/latency profile & MVP burst plan

Thanks — attached a small anonymized sample (syncstream_traffic_sample.csv) and a one-pager describing our expected demo/event windows. Answers inline:

- Prompt mix: ~70% short templates (20–80 tokens), ~20% medium retrieval prompts (150–400 tokens), ~10% long context (>500 tokens).
- Streaming: yes, we stream tokens to the web client for perceived responsiveness.
- KV cache: we expect to keep last 3 turns in-memory per session (~= 600 tokens average).
- SLA: p95 < 400ms is generation-only (model decode). End-to-end can tolerate additional network overhead.

Attachments: syncstream_traffic_sample.csv (CSV stub), event_windows.docx (short). Procurement is looping in a budget owner — procurement@syncstream.ai — for contractual questions.

Let us know if you need additional telemetry. Happy to schedule a 30m window Mon morning PT.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pre-commit sizing: traffic/latency profile & MVP burst plan

Cara — appreciate the sample and the clear answers. Summary of next steps / proposed pre-commit plan:

1) Preliminary sizing (attached): we recommend a medium reserved pool of 4x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (reserved) with a 2-GPU hosted fallback apron for extreme demo bursts. With your mix + KV cache (600 tokens/session) this maps to ~250 concurrent sessions at model p95 ≈ 350ms in our sim.

2) Operational knobs: session affinity ON (KV cache), streaming enabled, and pro-rated reserved + hosted fallback for regional failover.

3) Cost & procurement: Ben will follow up with an estimated monthly committed cost vs the reserved+burstable option. Expect a hubspot note and a DocuSign link for a 3-month pilot commitment if you want the reserved pool knocked in quickly.

4) Scheduling: proposed technical deep-dive Tue 10 AM PT (30m). If that works, I’ll send an invite with an agenda: sizing assumptions, sim output, and a short runbook for failover.

Quoted for transparency: Attached: mvp-burst-plan.xlsx (simulation workbook), syncstream_traffic_sample.csv (customer-provided). Shared links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/SS-2028-07-PRECOMMIT, DocuSign preview link above.

If that all looks good I’ll loop procurement on the timeline.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
